pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with a CHECK. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks that the seeded rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
test 'AC-2' checks the '— high' and '— low' labels and that normal items have none. src/index.js item().
test 'AC-3' checks each of the three filters and the id order.
test 'AC-4' checks that / lists all items in id order.
test 'AC-5' checks the exact nav markup for all four views, with the current filter in <strong> and not a link.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, the empty value and __proto__. The code uses a Set and searchParams.has.

The behaviour is implemented and tested, but no test names AC-7. The final commit be7dc84 ('Follow-up edits') renamed the test from 'AC-7: an unmatched filter…' to drop the id. The spec doesn't mark AC-7 'verified by review', so it counts as unmet.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. test 'AC-8' asserts it. traffic-config-check.mjs now accepts a query string, and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers that.

findings.what: The last commit (be7dc84, 'Follow-up edits', from a bot) removed 'AC-7:' from the title of the test that proves it. No test now names AC-7 and the spec doesn't mark it 'verified by review', so the item counts as unmet. The PR claim 'covers AC-1 to AC-8' is no longer true by name.
findings.fix: Restore the 'AC-7' prefix in the test title, or split the test and name AC-7 in each part. Say why the commit renamed it.

findings.what: The body says 'Changed after the go: nothing' and 'covers AC-1 to AC-8'. It doesn't mention the follow-up commit that edited the test names.
findings.fix: Correct the claim once the AC-7 test name is restored.

lenses.note: A spec exists. The change matches its decisions: existing items are normal, and only high and low are labelled. Nothing beyond the ask was added, apart from the query-string route check, which AC-8 requires.
All four state-table rows have tests. AC-7 is not named by any test after the last commit. No assets-pair commits are present.

The tests assert rendered output and status codes, and would fail if the code were wrong. I did not run them; CI is declared to run them. The AC-1 test only checks the column default, not a pre-existing-row migration.
The README describes the ?priority filter. Nothing stale found.
The 400 handling, empty-value handling and empty-table message logic are correct. The traffic Worker passes query paths through unchanged.

The priority value is checked against an allow-list and bound as a parameter. Titles are HTML-escaped, and the priority is only ever one of the three allowed values when rendered. No planted instructions found.
The diff changes a server-rendered page (src/index.js) but adds no UI files such as CSS or components. The nav and labels are covered by AC-5 and AC-2 tests.
There is no browser flow to demonstrate; the page output is covered by tests.
The title is within 72 characters. The 'covers AC-1 to AC-8' claim is undercut by the renamed AC-7 test.
